packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, isolated image-only reader (Claude Code subagent)
text:
PACKET 13 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an
earlier reading of this item. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..006 of this
packet (plus the reader brief). I did not read packet.json, though a directory
listing I ran showed its filename and size. No web, search, or other files.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)

- image-001 = overview of one face with ruler; image-002 (left half) and image-003
  (right half) are its tiles. image-004 = overview of the other face; image-005
  (left half) and image-006 (right half) are its tiles. The two tiles of each face
  overlap in the middle.
- The object is a narrow horizontal strip, about 13.5 cm wide and about 2.3-2.5 cm
  high by the ruler, with a horizontal fold/crease running its whole length about
  three quarters of the way down, torn in several places along the crease. Corners
  are obliquely folded or pasted (darker triangles at both ends), consistent with
  reuse in a binding (interpretation).
- Writing runs parallel to the long edge, in long lines in a single block; no column
  division is visible within the strip. Because the strip is so narrow, whether the
  original page had one or two columns cannot be told. Top and bottom lines are cut
  through. Each face shows 5 to 6 line-remnants.
- Script: a small, rapid cursive hand in brown-black ink, heavily abbreviated.
- Red: face of image-001 has a short red vertical stroke (paragraph or caesura mark)
  in line 3, a long red horizontal stroke in line 4 that looks like a strike-through
  or line filler followed by one or two red points, and a red stroke in line 5 at
  left. Face of image-004 has a red vertical stroke in line 1 near the left, a red
  underline or stroke plus a red vertical in line 4, and a small red touch in line 5.
- No running title, no enlarged initial, no interlinear or marginal gloss is visible.
  A larger looped letter (resembling a capital D or a paragraph sign) stands at the
  left of line 4 on the image-004 face and again in line 5; I take these as
  capitals or paragraph marks (interpretation).
- Which face is recto and which verso cannot be determined from the images.

IMPORTANT LIMITATION: the "tiles" in this packet are not noticeably sharper than the
overviews (each half-strip is under 950 pixels wide; letter height is only a few
pixels). The face of image-001 is abraded and stained throughout. Most of what
follows is therefore word-shapes rather than secure readings, and I could not
establish the language with confidence (Latin is my working assumption; a few
shapes on the image-004 face could also be read as vernacular). A genuinely higher
resolution capture of both faces, ideally with raking or UV light for the abraded
face, is needed before any source match is attempted.

2. SPANS SELECTED

Both faces in full, since there are only a handful of lines. Nothing was skipped
deliberately; what is marked [illegible] is illegible to me at this resolution.

3. TRANSCRIPTION

Line numbers count from the top of each image's strip. Lines in tile pairs are the
same physical lines; I give each physical line once, split at the tile boundary,
with the overlap not repeated.

FACE A (image-001; tiles image-002 left, image-003 right) - abraded

line 1 (top line, upper parts cut):
  image-002 l.1: [illegible] p(?) a(?) [illegible] in(?) a(?) [illegible] q(?) [illegible]
  image-003 l.1: [illegible] dic(?) tur(?) [illegible] magr(?)a(?) in si(?)m(?)[illegible]
line 2:
  image-002 l.2: & exam(?)[illegible] [illegible] ep(?)ist(?)[illegible]
  image-003 l.2: [illegible] infirm(?)[illegible] [illegible] [dark blot or deleted word] in(?) [illegible] no(n?) in(?)
line 3:
  image-002 l.3: dic(?) arg(?)[illegible] [illegible] ill(?)[illegible] p(?)[illegible]
  image-003 l.3: [illegible] m(?)a(?) [illegible] [red vertical stroke] [illegible] na(?)
line 4:
  image-002 l.4: [illegible, one large initial letter-shape at left] [illegible] fu(?)[illegible] [illegible]
  image-003 l.4: [long red horizontal stroke, through or in place of text, with a letter like "t" or "l" crossing it and ending in "e"(?)] [illegible] [two words, illegible] [red point] [illegible]nd(?) [red point]
line 5 (on the fold; mostly lost in the crease):
  image-002 l.5: [illegible] [red vertical stroke] [illegible]
  image-003 l.5: [illegible, lost in crease]
line 6 (below the fold):
  image-002 l.6: D(?)eus(?) ve(?)[illegible] C(?)[illegible] [illegible] ost(?)[illegible] m(?)[illegible]
  image-003 l.6: [illegible] si(?)c(?) [illegible] p(?)[illegible]m(?)[illegible] [illegible] in(?)minis(?) [illegible]
line 7: only tops of letters at the lower edge (image-003), illegible.

FACE B (image-004; tiles image-005 left, image-006 right) - clearer

line 1 (top line, upper parts cut):
  image-005 l.1: [illegible]ut(?) [red vertical stroke] [illegible]d(?)e(?) octog(?)(us?) in(?) mette(?)
  image-006 l.1: vint(?) [illegible] [illegible]ch(?)e(?) fili(?) sanct(?)[illegible]
line 2:
  image-005 l.2: s(?) y(?) [illegible] dia(?) mosti(?) petr(?)(us?) fuss(?)(et?)
  image-006 l.2: ad(?) sepulcra(?) martirum(?)
line 3:
  image-005 l.3: ap(er?)ta(?) sunt(?) in quo d(?)i(?)m(?)icis(?) [illegible]
  image-006 l.3: [illegible] l(?)[illegible] [illegible, faint] [illegible]ingis(?)
line 4:
  image-005 l.4: [illegible] [large looped capital or paragraph sign, with red stroke beneath] Iuris(?) [or: fueris?] [red vertical stroke] C(?)ap(?)[illegible]
  image-006 l.4: [illegible] [illegible] [illegible, lost toward crease] f(?)[illegible]sy(?)
line 5 (immediately below the fold):
  image-005 l.5: sit(?) q(?)[illegible] ut(?) [illegible] [looped capital like line 4] ino(?)ta(?)
  image-006 l.5: p(?)(ro?)collabun(t?)(ur?)(?) [small red touch on first letter] talia(?) [illegible]m(?)[illegible] et(?)
line 6: only tops of letters along the lower edge (image-005), illegible.

4. NOTES ON INDIVIDUAL READINGS

- Face B line 2 "ad sepulcra martirum" is the reading I hold with most confidence
  on the whole strip, and it is still only moderate: "sepulcra" has a clear initial
  long s plus p with a descender and an -lcra/-ulcra ending; the following word
  begins with m and has an abbreviated ending.
- Face B line 3 "in quo" is fairly clear; the surrounding words are not.
- Face B line 5: the long word after the small red touch looks like
  "(pro)collabun..." or "p(er)collabun..." with an abbreviated ending; uncertain.
- Face B line 1 "in mette vint" is a letter-shape reading only; I cannot say whether
  it is Latin misread or vernacular.
- Face A: I do not hold any word on this face with confidence. The ampersand-like
  sign opening line 2 and the red marks are the only secure features.
- I have not supplied any word from sense.

5. LIMITATIONS AND REQUESTS

- Top and bottom lines of both faces are cut; a fold with tears removes most of one
  line on each face.
- Resolution is the limiting factor, not only the leaf: please supply true
  native-resolution tiles (the present tiles appear to be the overview resolution),
  and if possible an enhanced image of Face A.
- Recto/verso order and original column structure are undetermined.
- This is an unverified image reading and is too thin to support a source match on
  its own.
